items.text: REFERRED TO CRIME VICTIMS, CRIME AND CORRECTION
REFERRED TO CRIME VICTIMS, CRIME AND CORRECTION

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S1352

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the correction law, in relation to services for
inmates of state correctional facilities upon their release therefrom


 PURPOSE :
Provides for notice of availability of services to prisoners upon
their release from state prison and for the making of arrangements
thereof.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
The correction law is amended by adding a new section 75, that will
require an exit interview for all inmates, to alert them to special
programs in their communities such as medical services, education,
alcohol or substance abuse treatment or mental health services.

 JUSTIFICATION :
In light of the fact that New York State is currently facing a
tuberculosis epidemic in its correctional facilities that is fueled by
poverty, homelessness and AIDS, it must become the primary charge of
this legislature to protect its civilian populations against this and
any other contagions.

This proposed legislation addresses the critical need for prisoners,
one in five of which is HIV infected and nearly that same proportion
tests positive for tuberculosis, to be made aware of the health and
educational services available to them in the communities they plan to
re-enter upon release. This action is necessary to both aid the
affected individual and to prohibit the escalation of epidemics
amongst our civilian populations as well. Epidemics will not be
restricted to urban centers. A recent study conducted by the Centers
for Disease Control found that 13 states-including Hawaii, Arizona and
Washington have recorded cases of Multi-drug resistant (MDR)
tuberculosis, during the first quarter of 1991 alone (MDR, was once
considered rare). So far, 90% of the cases have involved people with
HIV or AIDS. But, there is no reason to assume they are the only
individuals contracting the infection. Some of today's sufferers are
undoubtedly passing their airborne drug-resistant germs on to others.
In the past year alone, MDR bacteria has swept through two prisons and
several hospitals in New York and Florida, killing a guard, a dozen
inmates and scores of patients.

Another study, which was conducted by Harlem Hospital also illustrates
the critical need for this legislation. Harlem Hospital found that
only 11 of the unsupervised TB patients they studied completed
treatment once they were discharged. A staggering 89% drifted off
their pills and 27 were sick again within a year. We venture to guess
that these statistics will ring true for prisoners as well. It must be
our resolve to put soon-to-be released prisoners in touch with the
essential programs and services that will aid them and safeguard the
community against further injurious strains and swelling epidemics.

The focus of the New York correctional program has been geared toward
rehabilitation. To that end the state has developed a number of
programs for inmates and recently released offenders. Unfortunately,
many people are not aware of the programs that exist for them upon
release. To rectify this situation this bill proposes the
establishment of a formal exit interview to inform the inmates of
programs that exist in his/her community and where possible assist the
inmate in making arrangements to enter these programs.  This bill is
not intended to impede or delay the release of any individual, its
primary function is to assist individuals in obtaining the necessary
treatment and to help curb the spread of disease in New York.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT :
Minimal.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become a law.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
The correction law is amended by adding a new section 75, that will
require an exit interview for all inmates, to alert them to special

services, education, alcohol or substance abuse treatment or mental

JUSTIFICATION:
This proposed legislation addresses the critical need for prisoners,

is not intended to impede or delay the release of any individual, its
primary function is to assist individuals in obtaining the necessary
treatment and to help curb the spread of disease in New York.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT:
Minimal.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become a law.

summary: Provides for notice by commissioner of correctional services of availability of medical, educational and other services, including alcohol and substance abuse treatment, to prisoners upon their release from state prison.
